explicacion.en: Because conste is subjunctive, learners expect another subjunctive after it. But you are stating a fact, so the second verb is indicative: es.

texto.en: «Que conste que…» (literally “let it be on record that…”) is a fixed phrase you use to make sure the other person remembers a fact or your position. It carries a hint of warning: you accept something, but you do not want it to be forgotten that you disagree, that you warned them, or that something was not your fault. Le pago, pero que conste que no estoy de acuerdo = I'll pay you, but let it be known that I don't agree. Constar means “to be on record”, and conste is its present subjunctive, a kind of formal “let it be on record”. The verb after the second que is a plain indicative, because you are stating a fact: que conste que el proyector es nuevo, not que conste que sea nuevo.

titulo.en: Where it goes, and what it is not

texto.en: Que conste que usually opens a sentence or comes right after a pause or a comma: Está bien. Que conste que yo avisé. You can use it to accept a condition and still keep your position, which is useful when negotiating with a technician. It sounds firm, so keep it polite: use usted and, before it, the polite requests you already know, like ¿Podría componerlo hoy, por favor? Do not confuse it with consta de, which means “is made up of”: El curso consta de diez clases. And after conste you never add de: it is que conste que, not que conste de que.

contexto.en: A morning in 2031 at the Andes Vivos office. The projector in the meeting room stopped working, and a Técnico has come to look at it. Emma and the Técnico use usted with each other.

dialogo.texto: Buenos días, señorita García. Me dijeron que el proyector de la sala de reuniones no enciende. ¿Desde cuándo tiene el problema?

traduccion.en: Good morning, Miss García. They told me that the projector in the meeting room won't turn on. Since when have you had the problem?

dialogo.texto: Buenos días. Desde esta mañana. Ayer funcionaba bien, pero esta mañana lo quise encender y no pasó nada. Lo usamos casi todos los días en las reuniones con las comunidades. ¿Usted es especialista en proyectores?

traduccion.en: Good morning. Since this morning. Yesterday it worked fine, but this morning I tried to turn it on and nothing happened. We use it almost every day in the meetings with the communities. Are you a specialist in projectors?

dialogo.texto: Sí, trabajo con proyectores desde hace diez años. Déjeme ver. Primero voy a revisar el cable de conexión, porque a veces el problema es solo el cable.

traduccion.en: Yes, I've worked with projectors for ten years. Let me see. First I'm going to check the connection cable, because sometimes the problem is only the cable.

traduccion.en: It's not very serious. Yes, I have the spare part in my car. I'll give you the quote: the part costs thirty dollars and the work, ten. In total it is forty dollars. With that everything is included: the part, the work and the test of the device.

dialogo.texto: Está bien, acepto los cuarenta dólares. Pero que conste que el proyector tiene solo seis meses de uso.

traduccion.en: Fine, I accept the forty dollars. But let it be known that the projector is only six months old.

traduccion.en: I know, and it is a pity. But the manufacturer's warranty was for three months and it has already ended. That's why I have to charge you for the part.

traduccion.en: I understand. Also, let it be known that I need it today: at three we have an important meeting and without the projector I can't present anything.

titulo.en: Offering an alternative with en vez de

texto.en: En vez de means “instead of”. You use it to propose a change to an offer: En vez de pagar todo hoy, pago la mitad = Instead of paying everything today, I'll pay half. It is the natural way to make a concession or to suggest an alternative when you negotiate an estimate. En lugar de means exactly the same thing. After en vez de you can put an infinitive (en vez de pagar) or a noun (en vez de un repuesto nuevo). English often uses “instead of paying”, with -ing, but Spanish never uses the gerund here: not en vez de pagando.

If the person who does the second action is different from the person who does the first, use en vez de que + subjunctive: En vez de que lo cambie usted, lo cambio yo = Instead of you changing it, I'll change it. If the subject is the same, the infinitive is enough: En vez de pagar todo hoy, pago la mitad. Remember that the preposition de is always there: en vez de, never en vez que + infinitive and never en vez pagar. To propose a change politely, combine it with the conditional you already know: ¿Podríamos cambiar el presupuesto? En vez de cambiar todo, podríamos cambiar solo los delanteros.

contexto.en: A garage in Quito in 2031. Emma takes the Andes Vivos van to the shop before a visit to a community. The Mecánico gives her an estimate, and Emma proposes changes with en vez de. They use usted with each other.

dialogo.texto: Buenos días, señorita. ¿En qué puedo ayudarle?

traduccion.en: Good morning, miss. How can I help you?

dialogo.texto: Buenos días. Vengo con la camioneta de Andes Vivos. Los frenos hacen un ruido muy fuerte y el viernes tenemos una visita a una comunidad.

traduccion.en: Good morning. I came with the Andes Vivos van. The brakes make a very loud noise and on Friday we have a visit to a community.

dialogo.texto: ¿Desde cuándo hacen ese ruido?

traduccion.en: Since when have they been making that noise?

dialogo.texto: Desde hace dos semanas, sobre todo cuando voy rápido. Ahora el ruido es más fuerte y me da miedo manejar así.

traduccion.en: For two weeks, especially when I drive fast. Now the noise is louder, and I'm afraid to drive like this.

explicacion.en: In entregar the g needs a u before e to keep its hard sound: entregue. Without it, ge would sound like a strong h.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Cómo no me lo arregle hoy, busco otro taller.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Como no me lo arregle hoy, busco otro taller.

explicacion.en: Learners who have just met the accent in ¿cómo? put it everywhere. Here como is a conjunction and has no accent.

texto.en: You already know si + present: Si no me lo arregla hoy, busco otro taller. Spanish has a firmer way to say the same thing: como + present subjunctive. Como no me lo arregle hoy, busco otro taller = If you don't fix it for me today, I'll look for another garage. It states a condition about the future and carries a warning: you are making a counteroffer with a limit. The consequence goes in the present or the future: no lo compro, me voy, buscaré otro taller. The condition can be negative (como no me lo entregue el jueves) or affirmative (como me lo deje en ciento veinte).

Como + indicative gives a reason, not a condition: Como llueve, nos quedamos en el taller = Since it is raining, we stay at the garage. Como + subjunctive sets a condition that has not happened yet. Only the verb tells them apart, so check it: arregle is subjunctive, arregla is indicative. The subjunctive forms are the ones you know: usted and él / ella share the same form. Entregar becomes entregue, with gu, to keep the hard g. Como has no accent here: you only write cómo in questions and exclamations. The tone is a firm pressure, so use usted and stay courteous.

objetivo.en: Haggle over the price at a crafts market with the usual formulas and close the purchase.

traduccion.en: to haggle, to bargain

nota.en: Say “rreh-gah-teh-AHR”: the first r is rolled. The noun is el regateo. In crafts markets, regatear is normal and polite.

traduccion.en: the woven item, the textile

nota.en: Say “teh-HEE-doh”: the j is a strong h. Tejidos covers scarves, ponchos and anything woven.

traduccion.en: the shawl (a Mexican word)

nota.en: Say “rreh-BOH-soh”: the first r is rolled and the z sounds like s. Rebozo is the Mexican word. In Otavalo and in Ecuador people say chal, chalina or bufanda, so here you only need to recognize it.

traduccion.en: alpaca (the animal and its soft wool)

nota.en: Say “ahl-PAH-kah”. Una bufanda de alpaca = an alpaca scarf.

traduccion.en: the vendor, the merchant (female)

nota.en: Say “koh-mehr-SYAHN-teh”: the c before i sounds like s. The word has one form for men and women: el comerciante, la comerciante.

traduccion.en: the awning, the market stall

nota.en: Say “TOHL-doh”. In a market, the toldo is the canopy over a vendor's stall, so people also use it for the stall itself.

traduccion.en: the little discount

nota.en: Say “rreh-bah-HEE-tah”. The ending -ita makes the request sound gentle. Rebaja is the plain word for a discount.

traduccion.en: the last price, the lowest price

nota.en: Say “OOL-tee-moh PREH-syoh”. Último has a written accent on the u.

traduccion.en: the sum, the total

nota.en: Say “SOO-mah”. ¿Cuál es la suma? = What is the total?

traduccion.en: to take (something) with you, to buy it

nota.en: Say “yeh-BAHR-seh”: the ll sounds like the y in “yes” and the v like b. Me lo llevo = I'll take it; me las llevo = I'll take them.

traduccion.en: the final purchase, the closing of the sale

nota.en: Say “KOHM-prah fee-NAHL”.

explicacion.en: English “you” works for everyone, so learners use tú. With a vendor you do not know, use usted: ¿me hace una rebajita?
English “the least” suggests el menos. Here Spanish uses the neuter lo: lo menos, which means “the least it can cost”.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Si llevaré doce, ¿me hace un descuento?
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Si llevo doce, ¿me hace un descuento?

explicacion.en: Because the purchase is in the future, learners add the future. After si, Spanish uses the present: si llevo doce.

texto.en: In a crafts market like the one in Otavalo, the first price is only the start: people expect you to haggle, and doing it politely, with a smile, is part of the game. The most common formulas are ¿Me hace una rebajita? (could you give me a little discount?), ¿Cuánto es lo menos? (what is the lowest you'll take?) and ¿Cuál es su último precio? The ending -ita in rebajita is a diminutive of courtesy: it makes the request sound small and gentle. You can also give a reason for the discount: Si llevo doce, ¿me hace un descuento? To close the deal you say Está bien, me lo llevo or Trato hecho. Use usted with the vendor: hace, never haces.

Lo in lo menos is neuter, so it never changes: ¿Cuánto es lo menos?, not el menos. After si use the present, even if you will buy later: Si llevo doce, not si llevaré doce. Llevarse means to take something with you, so it is the verb for buying and leaving with it: Me lo llevo = I'll take it; me las llevo = I'll take them (feminine plural, like las bufandas). The vendor answers with fixed phrases too: Se las dejo a nueve dólares = I'll let you have them for nine dollars, and Es mi último precio = that's my last price. If both sides give a little, you reach a deal.

explicacion.en: El de means “the one of” and needs a masculine noun already mentioned. To bring back a topic, use the neuter lo: lo de la fecha.

titulo.en: Going back to a topic with lo de

texto.en: Lo de + noun lets you bring back a topic you have already discussed without repeating it: lo del precio, lo de la fecha, lo del pago. It means “the matter of the price”, “what we said about the date”. It is very useful when you close a deal: you go through each point one by one, as in Entonces, lo del precio queda en ochenta dólares. You can also use it with an infinitive: lo de pagar en dos partes = the idea of paying in two parts. And it can point to something that happened: lo de ayer = what happened yesterday.

titulo.en: Lo never changes, and de joins the article

texto.en: Lo is always lo, even when the noun is feminine or plural: lo de la fecha, lo de los cables. What changes is the preposition: de + el becomes del, so you say lo del precio and lo del pago, never lo de el precio. With la, los and las, de stays separate: lo de la fecha, lo de las piezas. And you always need de: not lo precio. Do not confuse it with el de, which means “the one of” and needs a masculine noun already mentioned. You will hear lo de after sobre, con and entre other words: Sobre lo del precio…, ¿Qué hacemos con lo del pago?
